title: feat(mwb): add option to reverse remote scroll direction on remote machines

review.body_prefix:
### Qualified current-revision assessment

The new option changes only vertical wheel messages in the remote-forwarding branch. It defaults to off, leaves local scrolling unchanged, and preserves horizontal-wheel and XBUTTON payloads. The existing input hook supplies a Windows message ID in `dwFlags`; it is not a combined bitmask. Its signed high-word wheel-delta producer also does not produce the hypothetical `int.MinValue` negation case.

The internal helper is already accessible to the tests through the existing `InternalsVisibleTo("MouseWithoutBorders.UnitTests")` declaration. No public API exposure or parameter/enum refactor is required for this change.

**Independent focused validation:** The exact affected Mouse Without Borders project builds with analyzers enabled and zero errors or warnings. All three new scroll helper tests pass, covering default-off behavior, signed vertical reversal, and unchanged horizontal-wheel/XBUTTON/move messages. The settings property, default, JSON conversion, two-way binding and existing save notification were source-traced.

No additional actionable correction is established in this scope. The author's Debug/Release, restart, mouse/touchpad and user/service two-machine results remain attributed author evidence. This assessment does not claim an independently executed Settings UI, persistence round-trip, physical two-machine scroll test or unconditional approval.

**Follow-up assessment:** The repeated internal-access concern is already satisfied by the existing friend-assembly declaration and the actual successful test build. Renaming the existing message-bearing parameter is optional; its actual producer and behavior remain unchanged. The same three-test execution receipt retains its exact revision identity.
